text:
Anya: Heads up — Product wants to GA Pegasus-XL next Tue. They shared a traffic sketch that looks heavier than previous launches. Need quick capacity sanity check.

Raj: Can you paste the traffic sketch? numbers matter.

Anya: From PM: 'expect 2.5x baseline peak for first 48h, per-request tokens ~700-1200 depending on prompt, concurrent tenants ~40% of customers will opt-in day 1'. I ran a rough calc this morning.

Kevin: ok rough math please.

Anya: Rough projection (using current batching + 16k kv cache):
```
- baseline token/sec (all models): 48k
- Pegasus-XL incremental peak token/sec: +118k
- combined peak token/sec: ~166k
- estimated GPU hours/day (current pack size & batching): 1,100 -> 2,520 (+129%)
- p95 latency contended: +40-80ms
```

infra-bot: forecast-run completed for 1774501234. Scenario: pegasus-ga, opt-in=40%, burst_profile=48h. Key outputs saved to /forecast/runs/1774501234.

Lina: EU-west has the tightest quota; we only have 28 GPUs reserved in that region. If traffic is global, routing policy will push more into us-west and increase cross-region egress.

Raj: So immediate asks: 1) how many extra GPUs needed to keep p95 < 350ms globally? 2) cost delta for 48h surge and monthly if steady? 3) any network egress hotspots?

Kevin: I ran a micro-sim this afternoon (4x smaller tenant set) — to keep p95 under 350ms for the modeled mix we need ~320 A100-equivalent GPUs total, which is about +140 GPUs over baseline. In EU-west specifically add ~24 GPUs to avoid cross-region fallback.

Anya: Cost calc?

Kevin: Quickbacks:
- 48h surge incremental infra cost ≈ $82k (spot-weighted estimate)
- Monthly if sustained (not likely) ≈ $1.9M incremental
- Autoscaling with reserved buffer reduces burst cost by ~28% vs pure on-demand spot mix

Oliver: Are there config levers to reduce GPU count without hurting latency? quantization? batching? lower context?

Kevin: Yes — options with rough impact:
- aggressive quantize -> -25% GPU needed but needs validation for quality
- enable prefix caching per-tenant -> -18% token work for repeated prompts
- increase batch window from 10ms -> 18ms -> +8% latency but -12% GPU need
- fall back to Pegasus-Lite (smaller variant) for non-critical tenants -> reduces peak by ~30%

Lina: Ops constraints: EU procurement can't get extra reserved capacity that quickly; spot pools are available but volatile. We'll need to combine cross-region routing with graceful degradation rules.

Raj: Action items:
- Kevin & Lina: run fast validation of quantized Pegasus-XL (quality + perf) by EOD today.
- Kevin: run a tighter simulation with per-region queuing by 10:00 tomorrow.
- Anya: coordinate with Product to announce staged rollout + opt-in gating for first 48h.
- Oliver: prepare fallback configs (Pegasus-Lite + batch window tweak) and an A/B policy.

infra-bot: created ticket INF-3187: "Pegasus-XL GA capacity run & fallbacks" assigned to Kevin, Lina, Oliver.

Anya: Also, note we should set a hard guardrail in Console to divert >65% of traffic to dedicated pools if latency climbs past threshold.

Kevin: I'll prototype a routing policy patch and post results. If quantize checks out, we might cut the extra GPU need to ~95 GPUs and save ~36% on surge cost.

Lina: If anyone needs EU GPUs urgently, ping me; I can attempt an emergency spot allocation but it's not reliable.

Raj: Good thread. Keep updates here. If we hit red during the launch, use INF-3187 for triage. :thumbsup:
